title: Add a search page and /api/items?q= filter to Flask app
description: A Flask app lists items on an index page. Add a /search page with a form and a /api/items?q= query filter endpoint. Include tests for the new API endpoint.

task_spec.prompt:
Add two things to the Flask app:

1. GET /api/items?q=<query> — filter items by name (case-insensitive substring match). If q is absent, return all items. Return JSON list.

2. GET /search — render a search.html template that has a form (GET method, action=/search, input name=q) and shows matching items when q is provided. Fetch matches from your new API logic (not a separate HTTP call — reuse the filter function).

Add tests in tests/test_search.py:
  - test /api/items?q=widget returns both items
  - test /api/items?q=a returns only 'Widget A'
  - test /search returns 200
  - test /api/items?q=xyz returns empty list

All existing tests must still pass.
success_criteria: search.html has a form with input name=q
followup_prompts: Good. Now handle edge cases: what does the UI show when data is empty, loading, or an error occurs? Add those states and tests.
Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to verify the complete implementation. Fix any failures and confirm all UI states work correctly.

check_commands.lint: uv run ruff check src/ tests/ 2>/dev/null || true
